title: Rigveda 1.47: To Asvins
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 1.47: To Asvins: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 1.47 is a hymn of 10 verses addressed to Asvins. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 1, a collection of hymns by many families of poets. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 32r-33r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).

translation.original_ref: RV 1.47.1-7 (aṣṭaka 1, adhyāya 4, varga 1); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 32v
translation.original_text:
1a̱yaṁ vā̱m madhu̍mattamaḥ su̱taḥ soma̍ ṛtāvṛdhā | tam a̍śvinā pibataṁ ti̱roa̍hnyaṁ dha̱ttaṁ ratnā̍ni dā̱śuṣe̍ ||
2tri̱va̱ndhu̱reṇa̍ tri̱vṛtā̍ su̱peśa̍sā̱ rathe̱nā yā̍tam aśvinā | kaṇvā̍so vā̱m brahma̍ kṛṇvanty adhva̱re teṣā̱ṁ su śṛ̍ṇuta̱ṁ hava̍m ||
3aśvi̍nā̱ madhu̍mattamam pā̱taṁ soma̍m ṛtāvṛdhā | athā̱dya da̍srā̱ vasu̱ bibhra̍tā̱ rathe̍ dā̱śvāṁsa̱m upa̍ gacchatam ||
4tri̱ṣa̱dha̱sthe ba̱rhiṣi̍ viśvavedasā̱ madhvā̍ ya̱jñam mi̍mikṣatam | kaṇvā̍so vāṁ su̱taso̍mā a̱bhidya̍vo yu̱vāṁ ha̍vante aśvinā ||
5yābhi̱ḥ kaṇva̍m a̱bhiṣṭi̍bhi̱ḥ prāva̍taṁ yu̱vam a̍śvinā | tābhi̱ḥ ṣv a1̱̍smām̐ a̍vataṁ śubhas patī pā̱taṁ soma̍m ṛtāvṛdhā ||
6su̱dāse̍ dasrā̱ vasu̱ bibhra̍tā̱ rathe̱ pṛkṣo̍ vahatam aśvinā | ra̱yiṁ sa̍mu̱drād u̱ta vā̍ di̱vas pary a̱sme dha̍ttam puru̱spṛha̍m ||
7yan nā̍satyā parā̱vati̱ yad vā̱ stho adhi̍ tu̱rvaśe̍ | ato̱ rathe̍na su̱vṛtā̍ na̱ ā ga̍taṁ sā̱kaṁ sūrya̍sya ra̱śmibhi̍ḥ ||
translation.text:
1ASVINS, for you who strengthen Law this sweetest Soma hath been shed. Drink this expressed ere yesterday and give riches to him who offers it.
2Come, O ye Aṣvins, mounted on your triple car, three-seated, beautiful of form To you at sacrifice the Kaṇvas send the prayer: graciously listen to their call.
3O Aṣvins, ye who strengthen Law, drink ye this sweetest Soma juice. Borne on your wealth-fraught car come ye this day to him who offers, ye of wondrous deeds.
4Omniscient Aṣvins, on the thrice-heaped grass bedew with the sweet juice the sacrifice. The sons of Kaṇva, striving heavenward, call on you with draughts of Soma juice out-poured.
5O Aṣvins, with those aids wherewith ye guarded Kaṇva carefully, Keep us, O lords of Splendour: drink the Soma juice, ye strengtheners of holy law.
6O Mighty Ones, ye gave Sudâs abundant food, brought on your treasure-laden car; So now vouchsafe to us the wealth which many crave, either from heaven or from the sea.
7Nâsatyas, whether ye be far away or close to Turvaṣa, Borne on your lightly-rolling chariot come to us, together with the sunbeams come.

translation.original_ref: RV 1.47.8-10 (aṣṭaka 1, adhyāya 4, varga 2); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 33r
translation.original_text:
8a̱rvāñcā̍ vā̱ṁ sapta̍yo 'dhvara̱śriyo̱ vaha̍ntu̱ sava̱ned upa̍ | iṣa̍m pṛ̱ñcantā̍ su̱kṛte̍ su̱dāna̍va̱ ā ba̱rhiḥ sī̍dataṁ narā ||
9tena̍ nāsa̱tyā ga̍ta̱ṁ rathe̍na̱ sūrya̍tvacā | yena̱ śaśva̍d ū̱hathu̍r dā̱śuṣe̱ vasu̱ madhva̱ḥ soma̍sya pī̱taye̍ ||
10u̱kthebhi̍r a̱rvāg ava̍se purū̱vasū̍ a̱rkaiś ca̱ ni hva̍yāmahe | śaśva̱t kaṇvā̍nā̱ṁ sada̍si pri̱ye hi ka̱ṁ soma̍m pa̱pathu̍r aśvinā ||
translation.text:
8So let your coursers, ornaments of sacrifice, bring you to our libations here. Bestowing food on him who acts and gives aright, sit, Chiefs, upon the sacred grass.
9Come, O Nâsatyas, on your car decked with a sunbright canopy, Whereon ye ever bring wealth to the worshipper, to drink the Soma's pleasant juice.
10With lauds and songs of praise we call them down to us, that they, most rich, may succour us; For ye have ever in the Kaṇvas' well-loved house, O Aṣvins, drunk the Soma juice.
